caption: A certificate of deposit (CD) is a savings product that earns interest on a lump sum for a fixed period of time. CDs differ from savings accounts because the money must remain untouched for the entirety of their term or risk penalty fees or lost interest. CDs usually have higher interest rates than savings accounts as an incentive for lost liquidity. These days high yield savings accounts offer similar rates though, so do the research and see what option works best for you. #PersonalFinance #moneytips #financetips #personalfinancetips #savingmoney #savemoney

If you're trying to grow your savings but not sure where to start, CDs and money market accounts both earn more than a regular savings account, but they serve different purposes. Here’s the breakdown: Certificates of Deposit (CDs): • fixed interest rate, often higher than savings • funds are locked for a set term • best for: saving for a known goal or date (ex: moving, wedding, tuition) Top CD Rates (May 2025): • Marcus by Goldman Sachs  – up to 4.20% APY, $500 min deposit • Bread Savings – 4.35% APY, min deposit $1,500 • Synchrony Bank – 4.25% APY, great long-term options, no minimum deposit Money Market Accounts (MMAs): • variable rate, often competitive • you can access your money (some offer debit cards or checks) • best for: people who want flexibility without sacrificing too much interest Top MMAs (May 2025): • Vio Bank MMA – 4.36% APY, $0.01 minimum • Ally Bank – 3.60% APY, no monthly fees, highly rated • Discover Bank – 3.50% APY, check-writing & debit access included Final tip: Both are FDIC insured up to $250,000.
